briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East remains a high-tension environment, marked by significant geopolitical maneuvering and localized conflicts. The most critical development of the past 24 hours is Iran's explicit rejection of full reopening of the Strait of Hormuz without US concessions and compensation, alongside Israel's Prime Minister Netanyahu's categorical rejection of the 15-point Gaza peace plan and insistence on complete Hamas disarmament. These stances underscore deep-seated impasses threatening further escalation.

IRAN
Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian appointed Mohsen Rezaei, military advisor to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, as the new Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council (SNSC), replacing Mohammad-Baqer Zulkadr. Pezeshkian reported a 7-8 hour meeting with Mojtaba Khamenei discussing crucial national issues, though no visual evidence accompanied this claim, and initial reports of Rezaei's appointment were briefly retracted by state media, suggesting internal dynamics.

Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman, Esmaeil Baghaei, reiterated that no direct negotiations are ongoing with the United States, with communications limited to message exchanges via mediators. Iran is currently focused on talks with Oman to regulate shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Baghaei stated that the Strait will not be considered a safe or fully open international waterway as long as the US naval blockade and other violations persist, demanding the US cease these actions and provide compensation for damages. He asserted Iran's control over the Strait as leverage. Iranian officials claim their missiles possess advanced guidance capabilities, including mid-course trajectory changes, and that US advanced military technologies, including artificial intelligence, failed against Iran's "institutional resilience" during the recent conflict.

The Wall Street Journal reported that Iranian attacks have destroyed or damaged at least 42 US military aircraft and inflicted $13 billion in equipment and facility damages. Iran rejected Ukraine's claim that an attack on an Iranian vessel was unintentional and demanded compensation, threatening retaliation otherwise. Separately, Iran claimed to have shot down a Chinese drone belonging to Saudi Arabia in southern Iran, and an American MQ-9 drone over Sirik, southern Iran. Rosatom has begun returning Russian specialists to the Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant, with plans to increase personnel to 100 by autumn. President Pezeshkian claimed to have resolved issues related to internet access, which was previously intended to be permanently restricted. Senator Ted Cruz (US) advocated arming Iranian protestors to allow them to determine their own future rather than deploying US troops. Economically, Iran reported 120 million liters of fuel smuggled in the past four months, 85% of which was diesel. Tehran's building materials experienced inflation exceeding 100% year-on-year.

ISRAEL
The IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir and senior command convened a joint operational forum for a multi-arena intelligence and operational update. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu explicitly rejected the US-backed 15-point Gaza peace plan, vowing no withdrawal until Hamas is genuinely and completely disarmed of all weapons. A senior Israeli official refuted reports of Qatar and Turkey supervising Gaza operations post-conflict.

Israeli forces carried out extensive military operations. In southern Lebanon, Brigade 55 and Yahalom forces located and destroyed an underground Hezbollah tunnel and a significant cache of weapons, including Kalashnikovs, anti-tank missiles/launchers, artillery, and RPG rockets. Israeli artillery also shelled Bani Haiyyan and Hadatha in southern Lebanon. In the West Bank, the IDF issued an intent to confiscate and demolish the home of terrorist Duas Hassoun in Beit Amr, responsible for the March 21, 2026 attack that killed Yehuda Sherman. The village of Taybeh near Ramallah was declared a closed military zone. Allegedly, Israeli forces invaded Syria's Quneitra countryside with tanks and military vehicles. An Islamic Resistance in Syria group claimed missile attacks on an Israeli base in Al-Jazeera camp, Daraa.

On the home front, an Israeli cadet in a flight training course died by suicide at an Air Force base, contributing to at least 18 reported Israeli military suicides this year. Defence Minister Ben-Gvir warned against "conceited agreements" that would "put us to sleep" before future attacks. He also reportedly humiliated Palestinian detainees over their hunger, telling them, "This is not a hotel. You will die." Domestic police actions included the arrest of 22 undocumented individuals, seizure of weapons (rifle, pistol, IDF frag grenade, ammunition) in Julis, and the discovery of grenades in Ashkelon and North Tel Aviv, and a suspected frag grenade in Hadera, mostly linked to criminal activity. An IDF soldier was arrested on suspicion of involvement in a serious stabbing incident in Haifa. A 16-year-old from the Kokhav HaShahar outpost was arrested after evading security forces during a weapons search. A 16-year-old boy died in a rappelling accident at Keshet Cave, and a 20-year-old soldier, Roi Ziv-Nir, died.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Hamas formally reaffirmed its commitment to the 15-point ceasefire roadmap for the second phase, while Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu rejected it. Netanyahu's rejection highlights a growing disunity between the US and Israel regarding a Gaza peace plan. Israeli forces conducted heavy firing in northern Beit Lahia and Al-Zahra, west of Khan Yunis, in the southern Gaza Strip. These attacks resulted in seven Palestinian injuries, including a woman and a child, amid ongoing ceasefire violations.

The Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor warned that Israeli restrictions on aid networks are severely disrupting food and medicine deliveries, escalating the risk of famine in Gaza. A Palestinian prisoners' rights group called for a transparent investigation into the death of Gaza detainee Ihab Mohammed Abdul Qader Diab and broader Israeli abuses. In the West Bank, the Palestinian Journalists Syndicate documented 108 attacks by Israeli forces and settlers against Palestinian journalists in July. International forces are reportedly deploying along Gaza's "Yellow Line" in coordination with the Israeli military, with varied reactions from Palestinians regarding their potential role in providing safety versus supporting the occupation.

LEBANON
Israeli forces conducted several strikes and military activities in southern Lebanon. Artillery shelling was reported in Bani Haiyyan, and explosions rocked various towns. Israeli forces were also reported to have set buildings on fire in Hadatha. IDF's Brigade 55 and Yahalom forces successfully located and destroyed an underground tunnel and a substantial cache of Hezbollah weapons, including Kalashnikov rifles, anti-tank missiles and launchers, artillery, and RPG rockets. Hezbollah warned that the Israeli occupation constitutes a threat to all of Lebanon and urged national unity to defend the country's sovereignty. Lebanese media outlet Al Mayadeen reported that there are currently no plans for further negotiation rounds between Lebanon and Israel. Israel reportedly offered a civilian prisoner exchange in return for the remains of Jewish individuals buried in Beirut and Sidon. Military activity was also reported in the village of Sarbin in southern Lebanon.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Syria and Russia signed a Memorandum of Understanding outlining the future of Russian military bases in Tartus and Hmeymim, intending to reorganize Russia's presence along the Syrian coast following 18 months of negotiations. Syrian internal security forces announced the dismantling of an ISIS terror cell in Khan Arnabah, Quneitra province, located mere kilometers from the Israeli border, which was involved in collecting weapons and transferring explosive devices. Separately, Israeli forces reportedly invaded Syria's Quneitra countryside with tanks and military vehicles. The "Islamic Resistance in Syria" (Olou al-Bas) claimed to have launched missile attacks against an Israeli base in the Al-Jazeera camp, western Daraa countryside, and released footage of these attacks.

In Iraq, the government stated it had no prior knowledge of Saudi-American airstrikes on Hashd al-Shaabi positions and that the Prime Minister has instructed the Foreign Ministry to submit a protest note to the UN Security Council regarding these bombings. The Iraqi Interior Ministry closed 71 fake headquarters falsely attributed to Hashd al-Shaabi and warned that any unauthorized drones would be treated as terrorist acts under counter-terrorism regulations. Iraqi security forces are slated to assume control of positions currently occupied by International Coalition forces by September 30th. The Iraqi army conducted aerial bombardment using Cessna Caravan aircraft against ISIS hideouts within the Kirkuk operations command, destroying eight such locations. Protests erupted in Dhi Qar province, southern Iraq, against deteriorating electricity services, where security forces reportedly assaulted demonstrators. Harakat al-Nujaba, an Iraqi resistance movement, warned against perceived US economic dominance in Iraq, describing it as a guise for plundering national resources.

GULF STATES
Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan signed a "Mecca Pact," a defense agreement aimed at strengthening security cooperation and collective deterrence. Pakistan's Foreign Minister stated the agreement is purely defensive and not directed against any specific nation. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman interpreted this pact as a reflection of regional states' increasing distrust in US security assurances and a notable shift in regional perceptions.

Yemen's Houthis renewed missile and drone attacks on al-Mokha port in southern Yemen, with reports of at least seven fatalities and 30 injuries among Yemeni army personnel and civilians. The Houthis also claimed to have attacked Saudi Aramco facilities. Saudi Arabia continues to keep Jizan, Najran, and Abha airports closed due to ongoing Yemeni attacks. Saudi Arabia recently acquired 730 PAC-3MSE missiles for $9 billion. Separately, a Chinese drone, reportedly belonging to Saudi Arabia, was shot down in southern Iran.

Oman is engaged in negotiations with Iran concerning shipping routes in the Strait of Hormuz. Japan's Prime Minister, Takayichi Sanae, held a telephone conversation with Sultan Haitham bin Tariq Al Said, urging the restoration of security in the Strait, to which Sultan Haitham responded that Oman would consult with concerned nations. The United Arab Emirates (UAE) successfully thwarted advanced cyber attacks targeting its aviation, energy, and education sectors. In Saudi Arabia, a factory fire in the capital, Riyadh, resulted in the deaths of 16 Bangladeshi migrant workers.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Netanyahu Rejects Gaza Peace Plan:** Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu explicitly rejected the US-backed 15-point plan for Gaza, vowing no withdrawal until Hamas is genuinely disarmed of all its weapons.
2.  **Iran Appoints New SNSC Secretary:** Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian appointed Mohsen Rezaei, military advisor to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, as the new Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council (SNSC).
3.  **Iran's Hormuz Stance:** Iran stated it has no direct negotiations with the US and will not fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz without the US ceasing violations, lifting its naval blockade, and providing compensation for damages.
4.  **Mecca Defense Pact Signed:** Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan formalized a defensive "Mecca Pact" to enhance collective security cooperation and deterrence.
5.  **Houthi Attacks Intensify:** Yemen's Houthis resumed missile and drone attacks on al-Mokha port in southern Yemen, causing at least 7 deaths and 30 injuries, and also claimed attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities.
6.  **Hezbollah Infrastructure Destroyed:** IDF Brigade 55 and Yahalom forces located and destroyed a significant underground Hezbollah tunnel and weapons cache in southern Lebanon.
7.  **Syria-Russia Military Agreement:** Syria and Russia signed a Memorandum of Understanding to reorganize the Russian military presence and manage its bases in Tartus and Hmeymim.
8.  **Israeli Military Suicides:** An Israeli cadet died by suicide, bringing the total to at least 18 reported Israeli military suicides since the beginning of this year.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
The risk of escalation remains critically high, particularly concerning the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran's stringent conditions for full reopening clash with US efforts to maintain oil flow. The active flashpoints include southern Lebanon, with ongoing Israeli strikes against Hezbollah infrastructure, and Yemen, where Houthi missile and drone attacks persist against Saudi and Yemeni government targets. The categorical rejection of the Gaza peace plan by Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu signals a prolonged conflict in the Palestinian territories and deepens the diplomatic rift between the US and Israel. US CENTCOM Commander Brad Cooper's message to Israel regarding ending conflicts on three fronts indicates a US desire for de-escalation, while simultaneously leaving open Israel's option for action against Iran's nuclear and ballistic missile capabilities, defining a clear red line. Internal political divisions within Iran, particularly concerning negotiations with the US, introduce an element of unpredictability to future decisions. The reported cyber attacks against the UAE underscore the multi-domain nature of regional instability.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **United States** has adopted a "low key" approach towards Iran, as stated by President Trump, focusing on economic pressure and "semi-negotiating" while noting Iran's severe economic distress. A US official confirmed that approximately 8 million barrels of oil flow nightly from the Persian Gulf via the southern Strait of Hormuz, coordinated with the US military. CENTCOM Commander Brad Cooper conveyed a message to Israel urging an end to conflicts on three active fronts, while acknowledging Israel's right to act against Iran's nuclear and ballistic missile programs. New York Times reporting suggests the US war on Iran has depleted US weapon stockpiles. The US also expresses concern that Patriot missiles supplied to Ukraine could end up on the black market.

The **Mecca Pact**, a defense agreement between **Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan**, was described by Pakistan's Foreign Minister as purely defensive, aimed at collective deterrence and not directed against any specific country. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman, however, viewed this pact as indicative of regional states' growing distrust of US security promises.

**Japan's** Prime Minister, Takayichi Sanae, called on **Oman** to help restore security in the Strait of Hormuz, to which Sultan Haitham of Oman committed to consulting with relevant countries. Oman is also actively negotiating with Iran on regulating shipping routes in the Strait.

**Germany** is doubling its Federal Police's anti-drone force and expanding operational bases following a drone incident at Leipzig Airport.

The **EU's** global warming monitor reported that Western Europe experienced its hottest June and July on record this year.

In **Iraq**, the government will protest Saudi-American airstrikes on Hashd al-Shaabi positions to the UN Security Council, stating no prior notice was given. Iraq's Interior Ministry has also clamped down on unauthorized drones, declaring them terrorist acts, and is preparing to take over positions from the International Coalition by September 30th.

**Ukraine** continues its drone attacks on **Russia**, reportedly causing fires at an industrial facility in Tyumen province, hitting a refinery in Nizhnekamsk, and causing power outages in Russian-controlled Zaporizhzhia. Russia claims to have intercepted 285 Ukrainian UAVs within 12 hours. Ukrainian President Zelensky alleged that Russia is preparing to deploy 30,000-50,000 North Korean troops in Ukraine.

**Greenland** has escalated its warning to a US oil company linked to President Trump over unauthorized drilling equipment. A rights group in **Vietnam** filed a criminal complaint against an Israeli soldier for alleged war crimes in Gaza and Lebanon.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions are observed regarding the internal political situation in Iran. President Pezeshkian's claim of a 7-8 hour meeting with Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei stands in tension with independent channels reporting ongoing speculation about Khamenei's health or absence. The absence of any visual or audio evidence of this meeting, coupled with the brief retraction and subsequent reposting of official announcements about Mohsen Rezaei's appointment, suggests internal disagreements or a controlled narrative within the Iranian leadership.

Several claims remain unverified. The "Islamic Resistance in Syria" (Olou al-Bas) claims of missile attacks on an Israeli base in Daraa lack independent confirmation. The full extent and impact of Houthi attacks on Aramco facilities in Saudi Arabia are unclear from the provided messages. Details regarding alleged "Saudi-American airstrikes" on Hashd al-Shaabi positions in Iraq lack specific confirmation or denial from US or Saudi sources within this feed. Iranian claims of shooting down both a Chinese (Saudi-belonging) and an American MQ-9 drone require independent verification.

Propaganda indicators are present across multiple sources. Iranian statements emphasizing the failure of US artificial intelligence, the country's national unity, the advanced capabilities of its missiles, and the "erosion" of US military and moral standing appear designed to project strength and resilience for both domestic and international audiences. Similarly, Israeli Minister Ben-Gvir's alleged comments to Palestinian detainees, taunting them about hunger, could be interpreted as inflammatory rhetoric aimed at a domestic political base.

Reporting gaps exist concerning the specifics of the "15-point plan" for Gaza and the precise nature of the "disunity" between the US and Israel on this plan. Details about the Mecca Pact beyond its defensive intent are not fully elaborated. There is also a lack of information from Russian or Ukrainian sources regarding the alleged deployment of North Korean troops in Ukraine. The brief deletion and re-publication of official news about Mohsen Rezaei's appointment also point to underlying information control or internal political maneuvering not fully explained in the raw feed.
